text:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: PAGE: High ECC error rate detected on GPU node titan-07 in pool titanpool (dedicated for tenant NexaHealth). Error rate > 5% over 5m. Affected serving jobs: gpt-small-2048. IncidentID: INC-2005-23

samir (oncall): I'm on it. pulling metrics and nvml logs now

samir (oncall): running `ssh ops@titan-07` then `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC` to confirm

samir (oncall): nvml shows volatile ECC errors on GPU0 and GPU2, counters climbing over last 10m. temps/clock look normal.

kai (sre): tagging in. if ECC persists we should drain and replace. How many pods/replicas pinned to this host?

liza (solutions): Priya — customer on the call reported 502s and timeouts. They mentioned pinned replicas for latency-critical routes.

priya (am): Confirmed with NexaHealth: spike in 5xxs starting ~10:05 UTC, about 12-18% error rate on their prod endpoint. They're seeing failures on some model calls. They're on a dedicated pool (titanpool).

samir (oncall): Starting controlled drain to avoid cache poisoning and hard OOMs: `runtimesctl drain-node titan-07 --reason "ECC error spike" --grace 90s`

deploy-bot: job scheduled: drain-job-id=dnj-2005-17, eta=90s

samir (oncall): Routing: marking host as DRAINING in service discovery; new requests should bypass within next 30s. Existing requests will be allowed to finish up to grace period.

jules (eng-runtime): I'm spinning warm replicas on fallback pool for NexaHealth to avoid cold start: `scale-replicas --tenant NexaHealth --pool fallback-warm --replicas 4`

kai (sre): Initiating hardware replacement workflow. Created infra ticket HW-2005-487 -> replace board / run memtest on GPUs. ETA: 3h for physical swap (on-prem shop), 1.5h if cloud host reprovision.

samir (oncall): pasted nvml excerpt:
```
GPU 0:
  Volatile ECC errors: 412
  Aggregate ECC errors: 420
GPU 1:
  Volatile ECC errors: 2
GPU 2:
  Volatile ECC errors: 398
```

liza (solutions): Noting customer impact: NexaHealth requests are latency-sensitive; some requests retried by client causing duplicates. Priya, can you tell them we routed traffic to fallback and will patch once hardware replaced?

priya (am): Messaging NexaHealth now: "We're routing your traffic off the impacted host and provisioning replacement. You may see intermittent 502s for inflight requests. We'll update in 15m with progress." I'll post copy here.

samir (oncall): Quick mitigation: set `max_retries=1` for NexaHealth route to avoid duplicate downstream effects, and enable lightweight caching for common prompts. Command: `rbctl routing update --tenant NexaHealth --max_retries 1`

jules (eng-runtime): Also enabling KV prefix cache for NexaHealth on fallback nodes to reduce load: `kv-cache enable --tenant NexaHealth --ttl 300`

kai (sre): Coordinating with infra team to reprovision a new host or replace board. If cloud ephemeral, we should mark pool capacity to add a new instance first to keep capacity stable. Creating change: CHG-2005-991.

samir (oncall): Observability: opening a short-lived eval set to detect regressions after routing switch. `evals run --tenant NexaHealth --tests latency,errors --window 5m`

priya (am): NexaHealth responded: "Thanks. We see fewer errors but still occasional timeouts. Please keep us posted."

liza (solutions): Good. Keep them in the loop and offer to pause heavy batch jobs if needed.

deploy-bot: HW ticket HW-2005-487 updated: vendor dispatched technician, ETA 2h 40m.

kai (sre): Handoff plan: If issue persists after replacement attempt, escalate to eng-runtime (jules) for deeper memtest and model-level degradation mitigation. For now, mitigation is routing + replacement + retries/TTL changes.

samir (oncall): Leaving detailed notes for night oncall:
- IncidentID: INC-2005-23
- Root cause: High volatile ECC errors on titan-07 GPUs 0 & 2. Suspected degrading HBM or board.
- Actions taken: drained titan-07, routed traffic to fallback pool, scaled warm replicas for NexaHealth, reduced max_retries, enabled KV caching. Created infra ticket HW-2005-487 and change CHG-2005-991.
- Observed impact: NexaHealth 5xx rate peaked ~18%, now down to ~3-5% after routing.
- Next steps for next oncall: monitor ECC counters, verify replacement completes, run `memtest86` on replacement hardware, validate traffic stability for 30m before returning node to pool.

samir (oncall): tagging @kai for handoff — I'm handing this to you in 20 minutes once we confirm metrics stable.

kai (sre): I acknowledge handoff. Will watch the ECC counters and infra ticket. If errors reappear post-replace, I'll coordinate full tenant migration to a different dedicated host and escalate to HW vendor.

priya (am): I'll send a status email to NexaHealth summarizing current mitigations and ETA for hardware swap.

liza (solutions): Thanks team. Please post final closure note once infra confirms replacement and node is healthy. :white_check_mark:

IncidentBot: NOTE: incident still open. next automated check in 10m.
